Author: Allan Wick
Message:
feat(ci): secret-material lint for non-secret fields (ADR-0001 Pillar 3, WIC-879) (#62)

Fails CI when secret-shaped material (API keys, tokens, PEM private keys)
appears in a committed non-secret field — binding names, resource names,
labels, or any tracked file. Cheap insurance against a repeat of WIC-751,
where an Anthropic key leaked as a Worker binding name.

- Pure, unit-tested core: packages/api/src/lib/secret-scan.ts
- File-discovery CLI (git ls-files): packages/api/src/secret-scan.ts
- Prefix/shape patterns: ghp_, github_pat_, sk-ant-, AIza, AWS, Slack,
  Twilio, Cloudflare, PEM private keys; realistic-length suffix so
  placeholders (sk-ant-..., ghp_xxx) don't trip.
- Conservative high-entropy heuristic on config/manifest files only
  (ignores ids/SHAs/URLs) to keep false positives low.
- Findings point at file:line:col + offending field; redacted output —
  never echoes the raw secret.
- Allowlist: inline `secret-scan:allow` pragma or
  .github/secret-scan-allowlist.json.
- Wired into deploy.yml lint-and-test job; npm run scan:secrets.
- Docs: docs/architecture/secret-scan.md. 14 unit tests + fixtures
  (catches sk-ant- in a binding name; passes a clean config).

the PK-prefixed DOCX bytes and threw "Unexpected token 'P'".

POST /cover-letters/:id/export is only ever called by the browser
client which always wants base64 JSON to construct a Blob download.
Remove the content negotiation and always return the JSON response.

Description: Database/broker connection string with an embedded credential (userinfo form)
Author: Backend Agent
Message:
fix(api): bound the postgres-js initial connect loop in getDb() (WIC-2043)

A failed database connect re-dialled without bound on both Workers
branches, spending the whole 1000-subrequest budget before any handler
could report why. Production /health answered 503 "Too many subrequests
by single Worker invocation" in 4-6s on every request.

postgres@3.4.9 connection.js:441-458 takes `if (initial) return
reconnect()` -- setTimeout(connect, 0), no backoff, no ceiling, and the
query is never rejected. It needs a close with no accompanying `error`
event, which is exactly what the Cloudflare socket polyfill produces
when a host accepts and closes; an `error` would reach errored(), null
`initial` and stop the loop after one dial, which is why a plain Node
ECONNREFUSED is already bounded and this never reproduced locally.

Neither existing option could have bounded it: `max: 1` bounds the pool,
not one Connection's socket lifecycle, and `connect_timeout` is
cancelled by closed() and re-armed by connect() on every iteration, so
it cannot fire while dials keep failing fast.

Bound it from outside instead (db/connect-bound.ts): a deadline armed
with the pool and disarmed by the first ParameterStatus -- the earliest
proof a TCP connect and startup handshake completed. On expiry the pool
is ended with {timeout: 0}, which reaches terminate() and nulls
`initial`, and a circuit opens on the request context so nothing else in
the invocation re-enters the loop. Tearing the pool down is the part
that stops the dialling; rejecting the caller alone does not.

Measured against the polyfill's clean-close socket shape: main issues
428 dials in 500ms with the query still unsettled; this issues 1 and
rejects. Also corrects the comment above WORKERS_CONNECTION_OPTIONS,
which claimed a guarantee of "one wasted subrequest" that the code never
provided.

subrequest-budget.test.ts is preserved, not replaced -- the classifier
and the 503 + Retry-After: 5 shaping from #148 keep passing, and the new
deadline error is classified alongside them.

Does not create the production Hyperdrive binding, which needs a
Cloudflare token and stays with WIC-1916 / WIC-1386.

Message:
fix(api): bound the direct-DB connect loop that drains the Worker subrequest budget (WIC-1916)

Production has no Hyperdrive binding, so getDb() takes the direct-DATABASE_URL
branch and postgres@3.4.9's ceiling-less initial-connect loop (connection.js:
`if (initial) return reconnect()` -> setTimeout(connect, 0)) re-dials a refusing

budget is gone. That is the 8-14s "Too many subrequests" 503 on GET /health.

- db/connect-budget.ts: withConnectBudget() races a DB op on a wall clock and
  ends the pool (sql.end({timeout:0})) on timeout/failure, which rejects the
  query and halts the reconnect loop; an isolate-level breaker then short-circuits
  the direct branch before dialing, protecting the rest of the warm isolate.
- app.ts /health probe wrapped; worker.ts trips the breaker on exhaustion.
- test/connect-budget-breaker.test.ts drives getDb()'s Workers direct branch
  against a refusing socket and COUNTS DIALS (the layer PR #148 stubbed out).
- ADR-007: correct the private-CA hypothesis (ssl:'require' => rejectUnauthorized
  false, so cert trust cannot be the failing factor; fault is transport + retry).
